docs.presetsShuffles.component: The recipes a reorder can LOOK like — one shelf, in isolation, drop-in. A shuffle is three layers a game keeps apart: the ORDER (a seed through the kit's rng, or the server's word), the TRUTH (`reorder` — the same children in a new order), and the LOOK — a recipe here. A recipe is a pure function of `(index, count, progress, rest pose, group extent) → in-flight pose`, played by the one clock; at progress 1 it returns the rest exactly, so a shuffle ends with no jerk, and at its commit phase its pose does not depend on the seat, so the reorder underneath moves nothing on the glass.
Shown on a row of plain tokens, not cards, on purpose: a recipe is entity-agnostic — children by index, cards or tiles or dice. A fan of a hand is the cards preset's business.
import { installStockShuffles, permutation, reorder, seededRng } from "game-kit"
const order = permutation(hand.children.length, seededRng(seed))   // the truth, seeded
A game registers its own with `registerShuffle(name, { poseAt, commitAt })`; an unknown name plays `riffle` rather than throwing.
docs.presetsShuffles.riffle: The pack splits into two halves that part to either side FANNED — no piece hiding another — and zip back together onto the new seats, the halves alternating in time so the merge reads as teeth meshing. The half a piece belongs to is its ORIGINAL half; where it lands is wherever the new order seats it. Nothing is ever swapped: a node keeps its face from the first frame to the last, and with no pile there is no top piece for the reorder to change in plain view. `riffle({ reach })`: `group` (the default) keeps it all in the picture, watchable end to end; `glass` carries the halves off the edge, for a pack too deep to fan.
docs.presetsShuffles.overhand: The pack in three packets, each lifted off the desk in turn (a touch higher per packet), SPREADING while it is up, and dropped back onto the new seats — the shape of a hand pulling packets off the top and letting them fall. The spread is there for the riffle's reason: a packet held as a pile shows only its top, and a reorder changes which piece that is. `overhand({ reach })`: `group` (the default) keeps the packets in the picture; `glass` lifts them clean off the top.
docs.presetsShuffles.wash: Every piece scatters to a ring around the group, turning as it goes, and the ring gathers back onto the new seats — the tiles-on-a-table shuffle, for pieces that have no order to riffle. Each piece keeps its own spoke, so nothing hides anything. The radius is `wash({ radius })` in units; `0` (the default) works out a ring that just clears the group.
docs.presetsShuffles.shake: The group trembles — and all the while it trembles, the pieces keep landing on each OTHER'S seats: dice in a cup, tiles in a bag, the previous client's scramble. The permutation of a beat is drawn from the beat number, so it is a picture rather than a truth and it is the same on every frame and every machine; the tree's own reorder happens under the trembling, and the last quarter carries every piece home to the order it will keep. `shake({ strength })`: harder is a wider tremble and oftener changes of hand; `0` only trembles.
